 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Catcher Joey Bart was designated for assignment by the Chicago White Sox on Tuesday, Nov. 17. He didn't have to wait long — or move far — to find his next team.
 Robert Murray of FanSided reported Friday on Twitter/X that Bart is headed to the Chicago Cubs . Mark Feinsand of MLB.com reported Bart was claimed off waivers, which would indicate the Cubs aren't sending anything (either a player or cash) to the White Sox for the 29-year-old catcher.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Bart slashed .214/.305/.357 in 44 games in 2026, which he split between the White Sox, Atlanta Braves and Pittsburgh Pirates . The No. 2 overall pick in the 2018 MLB Draft by the San Francisco Giants , Bart has played 379 career big-league games for four different teams from 2020-26.
 MORE: Mets lose pitcher to Cubs two days after they signed him 
 Bart may supplant Kelly as backup catcher
 Atlanta Braves catcher Joey Bart (16) circles the bases on a two-run home run against the Pittsburgh Pirates at PNC Park. Mandatory Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters)
 Bart gives the Cubs a veteran backup to starter Miguel Amaya. They had no backup catchers on their 40-man roster after Carson Kelly became a free agent.
 Kelly, 32, slashed .258/.336/.376 for the Cubs in 2026, and was always likely to sign with a team that could offer more playing time in 2027 than the Cubs.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement While claiming Bart doesn't necessarily preclude the Cubs from bringing Kelly back, it appears even more likely that Kelly will be moving on.
 MORE: Cubs pitcher might not be ready for Opening Day after surgery 
 Bart had his best seasons in 2024 and 2025 with the Pirates after the Giants designated him for assignment.
 In 2024, he set career highs in home runs (13), RBIs (45) and slugging percentage (.462). In 2025, he set career highs in games (93), at-bats (285) and on-base percentage (.355).
 If Bart exceeds those numbers with the Cubs, it likely would come as a result of an injury to Amaya. If he doesn't, at least the Cubs have a logical backup in place.
